stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy reviews a Lomotil prescription and its dispensing history. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Lomotil is an unrestricted Schedule VI drug.
Massachusetts Schedule V refill limits apply.
Covered Schedule V dispensing is reportable to MassPAT.
The prescription remains refillable for one year.
The Schedule II 30-day validity rule controls each refill.

explanation.core_reasoning: The supported conclusions on these facts are: Massachusetts Schedule V refill limits apply. Covered Schedule V dispensing is reportable to MassPAT.

choice_analysis.A: Not supported: Lomotil is an unrestricted Schedule VI drug.
choice_analysis.B: Supported: Massachusetts Schedule V refill limits apply.
choice_analysis.C: Supported: Covered Schedule V dispensing is reportable to MassPAT.
choice_analysis.D: Not supported: The prescription remains refillable for one year.
choice_analysis.E: Not supported: The Schedule II 30-day validity rule controls each refill.

related_facts: diphenoxylate and atropine (Lomotil) is used for adjunctive therapy in the management of diarrhea; it is federal Schedule V and Massachusetts Schedule V.
A Massachusetts Schedule V prescription may not be refilled more than five times or later than six months after the prescription was issued.

Covered pharmacies report dispensing of Schedule II through V controlled substances and DPH-designated additional drugs, including gabapentin, to the Massachusetts PMP under the current submission standard.
explanation.mpje_trap: Distinguish this near-miss from the controlling rule: 'Lomotil is an unrestricted Schedule VI drug.'

reasoning_steps: Classify diphenoxylate and atropine under the federal and Massachusetts schedules before selecting a legal pathway
Match the scenario's operative facts to Massachusetts Schedule V prescription refill limits
Reject nearby rules whose schedule, trigger, deadline, or actor differs from Schedule V refills
